review: 1:1–2 is the two-line acclamation stanza the print puts before the four-line stanzas (tune 99.99 – 69.69); like tr0157/0177 it is kept as two lines and not padded, which is why the metre script will call it short by design.
2:3 גּוֹאֵל כָּל־בָּשָׂר — the Arabic فَادِي الْوَرَى; בָּשָׂר is kept as in Joel 3:1 so 'all flesh' remains the scope of the redemption.
2:4 פָּנָיו כַּשֶּׁמֶשׁ מְאִירוֹת — Rev 1:16 (וּפָנָיו כַּשֶּׁמֶשׁ הַיָּפֶה); the simile is kept as a simile and the plural פָּנִים takes a plural participle, which is the biblical agreement.

3:2 תְּהִלַּת תּוֹדָה — the Arabic حُلْوَ تَسْبِيحِ شُكْرٍ رَخِيم is a construct chain of three nouns ('sweet hymn of thanks'); the Hebrew keeps a chain (תְּהִלַּת תּוֹדָה) with two adjectives, rather than splitting it into a sentence.

4:3–4 יְגוֹן הַמָּוֶת … הֶעָמָל וְהַדְּוַי — the Arabic حُزْنُ الرَّدَى / الشَّقَا وَالْعَنَا; דְּוַי (Ps 41:4) is kept for الشَّقَا, a sickness-sorrow rather than generic tiredness, so the pair is sorrow and disease, not sorrow and work.
5:3–4 אֲדוֹן הָאֲדוֹנִים … אַרְיֵה גּוֹבֵר — Rev 19:16 with Rev 5:5; both are kept as titles in apposition, since the stanza ends by naming Him rather than describing Him.
